prompts.summarizeBody: Summarize the BIDS dataset I’ve opened — how many subjects, which modalities are present, and any obvious gaps. Don’t change anything yet.
prompts.runValidatorLabel: Run BIDS validator and report issues
prompts.runValidatorBody: Run the BIDS validator on this dataset and list the most actionable issues. Group them by severity. Don’t fix anything yet — just report.
prompts.findMissingTaskNamesLabel: Find missing TaskName fields and suggest fixes
prompts.findMissingTaskNamesBody: Look for func/*_bold.json files that are missing the TaskName field. For each one, suggest the correct TaskName based on the filename’s task entity. Show the proposed edits before applying them.
prompts.cleanupStubSidecarsLabel: Clean up empty or stub sidecars
prompts.cleanupStubSidecarsBody: Find sidecar JSON files in this dataset that are empty, contain only an empty object, or carry obvious TODO placeholders. Propose what to remove or fill in. Show me the proposed edits before applying them.
prompts.checkParticipantsBody: Compare participants.tsv against the sub-* folders on disk. Report subjects that are in one but not the other, and propose how to reconcile them. Don’t edit anything yet.
prompts.renameSubjectBody: I want to rename one subject from <FROM> to <TO> across folders, participants.tsv, *_scans.tsv, and any IntendedFor references. Use the rename_entity tool — don’t edit participants.tsv by hand. Show me what will change before applying.
prompts.minimizeBody: Tidy up this BIDS dataset by removing redundant entities. First list what is removable with the remove_entity tool reasoning (e.g. a single session that can be collapsed, or a run-1 present on every scan). Explain each proposed removal and what it touches, then propose them one at a time for me to approve. Do not change file contents beyond the entity cleanup.
prompts.findDatesLabel: Find dates that could re-identify subjects
prompts.findDatesBody: Scan this dataset for anything that looks like a date and could help re-identify a participant before I share it. Check: every sub- subject label, every ses- session label, the participant_id and any columns in participants.tsv, the acq_time column of every *_scans.tsv, *_sessions.tsv, and the JSON sidecars (e.g. AcquisitionDateTime, AcquisitionTime, fields containing a patient name or ID). Important: BIDS recommends shifting de-identified dates to the year 1925 or earlier, so in *_scans.tsv acq_time treat any year AFTER 1925 as a real (unshifted) scan date and flag it (a year of 1925 or earlier is an intentionally shifted date and is fine). Report each match with its file/label and why it looks like a date (a real acq_time year > 1925, numeric YYYYMMDD, timestamps, or month names like '28April20'). List findings only — do not change anything; I will decide what to fix.
prompts.authorEventsLabel: Create or modify task events files
prompts.authorEventsBody: Help me author BIDS task events files for the functional runs in this dataset. First use list_files and read_file to see which task-*_bold runs lack an _events.tsv, and read any existing _events.tsv and the task-*_bold.json for context. Do NOT invent onset or duration values: ask me for the task timing (or paste a stimulus log for you to transcribe) before writing any rows. An _events.tsv must have at least the onset and duration columns, usually with trial_type too. Write events files with save_text_file, and write column descriptions or a missing TaskName with save_sidecar; use rename_entity if a task label needs changing. Resting-state (task-rest) runs legitimately have no events, so do not force them. Propose each write for me to approve before it runs.

share.whereIsTokenIntro: Brainlife issues a token from a single page — no DevTools or CLI required:
share.whereIsTokenStepBrowser: Click "Open browser to sign in" above to open brainlife.io/settings/account. If you are not already signed in, brainlife will redirect you through your preferred sign-in method (Google, ORCID, Globus, GitHub, native, or LDAP) and return you to the settings page.

share.whereIsTokenStepDocs: brainlife.io/docs is the canonical reference if the settings page moves.
share.openneuroWhereIsTokenSummary: Where do I find my OpenNeuro API key?
share.openneuroWhereIsTokenIntro: OpenNeuro issues an API key from a single page:
share.openneuroWhereIsTokenStepBrowser: Click "Open browser to sign in" above — OpenNeuro will redirect you through ORCID or Google, then display a long key (three segments separated by dots) at openneuro.org/keygen.
share.openneuroWhereIsTokenStepDocs: docs.openneuro.org is the canonical reference if the keygen page moves.
share.openneuroCreateBlurb: OpenNeuro assigns a fresh accession (ds00XXXX) automatically. Confirm the dataset name + initial version below, then tick at least one affirmation.
share.openneuroSnapshotHint: Creates a tagged snapshot on OpenNeuro immediately after upload. Leave blank to skip — you can snapshot later from the OpenNeuro UI.

share.openneuroAffirmHint: Tick at least one box. OpenNeuro requires one of these affirmations on every new dataset.
share.ebrainsWhereIsTokenSummary: Where do I find my EBRAINS token?
share.ebrainsWhereIsTokenStepBrowser: Click "Open browser to sign in" above — lands on query.kg.ebrains.eu.
share.ebrainsWhereIsTokenStepProfile: Click your profile icon (top-right) → "Copy token to clipboard". Paste it here.
share.ebrainsWhereIsTokenStepTTL: Tokens expire after ~30 minutes — re-paste when the TTL chip lapses.
